name: MATHVISTA
description: MATHVISTA is a benchmark dataset for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It aggregates 6,141 examples from 31 sources (28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created: IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA), covering seven reasoning types (algebraic, arithmetic, geometry, logical, numeric commonsense, scientific, statistical), five task types (FQA, GPS, MWP, TQA, VQA), and 19 visual contexts with fine-grained metadata (question/answer type, task, grade level, context, reasoning tags).
inLanguage: Primarily English with 6.57% non-English (including Chinese and Persian)
publisher: ICLR 2024 (conference paper); dataset hosted at project website
citeAs: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao. MATHVISTA: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. ICLR 2024.

creator.name: UCLA; University of Washington; Microsoft Research

rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataCollection: Compiled nine math-targeted multimodal datasets (e.g., Geometry3K, UniGeo, GeoQA+, CLEVR-Math, IconQA, TabMWP, SciBench, TheoremQA), and 19 VQA datasets with math-related instances filtered via heuristics (numeric answers and quantity words), then human-validated. Additionally created three new datasets: IQTest (logical puzzles from online learning platforms), FunctionQA (questions about function plots), and PaperQA (questions from scientific figures/tables/charts of papers, sourced from HuggingFace papers released Aug 2023). Each source capped at 400 examples; metadata automatically derived/verified. The full benchmark is split into testmini (1,000) and test (5,141); deterministic accuracy evaluation with LLM-based answer extraction.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA figures sourced from papers released in August 2023; GPT-4V evaluation conducted Oct 7–15, 2023; Bard captioning Sep 8–10, 2023. Broader collection timeframe for other sources not explicitly stated.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk used for human performance and Bard assessment; custom internal GUIs for labeling math-related instances, reasoning types, and annotating new datasets.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:annotatorDemographics: Human performance annotators required >5,000 HITs on AMT, >0.99 acceptance rate, and at least high school diploma; newly created datasets’ questions annotated by graduate students in STEM; three expert annotators labeled math-related instances and reasoning tags. Inter-annotator agreement: Fleiss’ kappa 0.775 for math-involvement; 99.2% consistency among new dataset annotators with only 6 disagreements out of 736.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and analyzing mathematical reasoning in visual contexts for LLMs/LMMs; evaluating across tasks, reasoning types, visual contexts, and grade levels; fostering development of general-purpose multimodal AI with robust math+vision reasoning; leaderboard and online evaluation for progress tracking.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Some items include natural images with people (e.g., VQA sources) and celebrity identification (e.g., age gap questions); models like Bard had restrictions on people images. No explicit collection of personal identifiers; sensitive content handling beyond source datasets’ original terms not detailed.
